# sub

> Subtract two 64-bit unsigned integers.

<section class="intro">

</section>

<!-- /.intro -->

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```javascript
var sub = require( '@stdlib/number/uint64/base/sub' );
```

#### sub( a, b )

Subtracts two 64-bit unsigned integers.

```javascript
var Uint64 = require( '@stdlib/number/uint64/ctor' );

var a = new Uint64( 10 );
var b = new Uint64( 5 );

var v = sub( a, b );
// returns <Uint64>[ 5n ]
```

#### sub.assign( ah, al, bh, bl, out, stride, offset )

Subtracts two 64-bit unsigned integers and assigns results to a provided output array.

```javascript
var Uint32Array = require( '@stdlib/array/uint32' );

var out = new Uint32Array( 2 );
var v = sub.assign( 0, 10, 0, 5, out, 1, 0 );
// returns <Uint32Array>[ 0, 5 ]

var bool = ( out === v );
// returns true
```

The function supports the following parameters:

-   **ah**: high 32-bit word of the first 64-bit unsigned integer.
-   **al**: low 32-bit word of the first 64-bit unsigned integer.
-   **bh**: high 32-bit word of the second 64-bit unsigned integer.
-   **bl**: low 32-bit word of the second 64-bit unsigned integer.
-   **out**: output array.
-   **stride**: stride length for `out`.
-   **offset**: starting index for `out`.

#### sub.strided( a, sa, oa, b, sb, ob, out, so, oo )

Subtracts two 64-bit unsigned integers stored in integer-valued strided array views and assigns results to a provided strided output array.

```javascript
var Uint32Array = require( '@stdlib/array/uint32' );

var a = new Uint32Array( [ 0, 10 ] );
var b = new Uint32Array( [ 0, 5 ] );
var out = new Uint32Array( 2 );

var v = sub.strided( a, 1, 0, b, 1, 0, out, 1, 0 );
// returns <Uint32Array>[ 0, 5 ]

var bool = ( out === v );
// returns true
```

The function supports the following parameters:

-   **a**: first 64-bit unsigned integer strided array view containing interleaved 32-bit unsigned integer high and low order words.
-   **sa**: stride length for `a`.
-   **oa**: starting index for `a`.
-   **b**: second 64-bit unsigned integer strided array view containing interleaved 32-bit unsigned integer high and low order words.
-   **sb**: stride length for `b`.
-   **ob**: starting index for `b`.
-   **out**: output array.
-   **so**: stride length for `out`.
-   **oo**: starting index for `out`.

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<!-- Package usage notes. Make sure to keep an empty line after the `section` element and another before the `/section` close. -->

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   When `b` is greater than `a`, the operation wraps around modulo `2^64` (i.e., `a - b + 2^64`).

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

<!-- eslint no-undef: "error" -->

```javascript
var Uint64 = require( '@stdlib/number/uint64/ctor' );
var sub = require( '@stdlib/number/uint64/base/sub' );

// Subtraction beyond JavaScript's safe integer limit (10^18 > 2^53 - 1):
var a = new Uint64( 1e18 );
var b = new Uint64( 1 );
var v = sub( a, b );
console.log( '%s - %s = %s', a.toString(), b.toString(), v.toString() );
// => '1000000000000000000 - 1 = 999999999999999999'

a = new Uint64( 1e18 );
b = new Uint64( 2 );
v = sub( a, b );
console.log( '%s - %s = %s', a.toString(), b.toString(), v.toString() );
// => '1000000000000000000 - 2 = 999999999999999998'

// Modular underflow wrap-around (modulo 2^64):
a = new Uint64( 0 );
b = new Uint64( 1 );
v = sub( a, b );
console.log( '%s - %s = %s', a.toString(), b.toString(), v.toString() );
// => '0 - 1 = 18446744073709551615'

a = new Uint64( 5 );
b = new Uint64( 10 );
v = sub( a, b );
console.log( '%s - %s = %s', a.toString(), b.toString(), v.toString() );
// => '5 - 10 = 18446744073709551611'
```

</section>
